title: Evolution varies the whole body in correlation, not character by character

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Evolution varies the whole body in correlation, not character by character

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Because dissimilar related fishes can be referred as wholes to the same figure in different coordinate systems, variation has proceeded on definite and orderly lines under a comprehensive law of growth affecting the whole structure, rather than by independent variation of separate parts as the usual conception of natural selection assumes.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. XVII: On the Theory of Transformations, or the Comparison of Related Forms

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: But if, on the other hand, diverse and dissimilar fishes can be referred as a whole to identical functions of very different co-ordinate systems, this fact will of itself constitute a proof that variation has proceeded on definite and orderly lines, that a comprehensive “law of growth” has pervaded the whole structure in its integrity

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter XVII, “On the Theory of Transformations, or the Comparison of Related Forms”; topic “Theory of transformations”. Scope: evolutionary differentiation of related animal species

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch17-03: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.58

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Existing morphology can test whether a global transformation summarizes variation. The asserted proof of a comprehensive growth law and contrast with natural selection do not follow uniquely from geometric fit, limiting discrimination.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Fit low-dimensional whole-body deformation models and modular independent-trait models to related-species morphometrics, comparing out-of-sample fit. Superior global fit tests coordinated variation but not a unique causal growth law.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Natural selection does not require character independence.

A compact transformation does not prove a developmental cause.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Whole-body transformations versus modular shape change can be compared on open images and scans. That tests the pattern half of the claim. It does not test the historical assertion that the pattern rules out natural selection, because selection is compatible with correlated change across the body.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Fit related species with a low-dimensional coordinate transformation of the whole body and with a model of independent regional changes, and compare held-out landmark error. A large advantage for the global transformation would support an integrated law of growth; the morphological fit would still leave natural selection unrefuted unless selection is separately shown to require part-by-part independence.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
A good global fit is also what selection on an integrated phenotype would produce.

Thompson's rival, independent variation of separate parts, is a historical picture of selection rather than a distinct morphological null.
